title: Zero-touch instrumentation gateway for background and batch jobs
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: A large fraction of customer-facing errors and latency spikes originate in background workers (cron jobs, batch pipelines, scheduled tasks). These jobs often run detached from the HTTP request path and either emit no tracing data or emit fragmented traces lacking provenance, making root-cause analysis and SLO attribution difficult.

Proposal: Implement a zero-touch instrumentation gateway and lightweight worker-side agent that lets background job orchstrators and task queues propagate a minimal trace envelope at job enqueue time, and ensures reliable, low-overhead span emission at job completion. The gateway provides a small HTTP/gRPC endpoint for orchestrators to attach canonical provenance metadata to jobs; the worker agent consumes that envelope, rehydrates a trace context, and emits child spans to Redwood's tracing backend.

Goals:
- Restore end-to-end trace continuity for scheduled/batch work with minimal SDK changes for customers.
- Provide sampling hints and a deferred-emit policy so high-volume batch pipelines don't overwhelm tracing ingestion.
- Support common orchestrators: Kubernetes CronJobs, Airflow, Celery, Sidekiq, Fargate scheduled tasks.
- Instrumentation should be opt-in per-namespace with sensible defaults for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
- Enqueue-time API and worker agent prototype implemented and tested end-to-end for Celery and Kubernetes CronJobs.
- Trace continuity validated in staging (parent request -> job -> post-job HTTP callback) for 95% of test traces.
- New dashboards: background-job-latency, job-error-rate-by-queue, and deferred-span-emit-queue-depth.
- Rollout plan and migration docs for customers, and migration playbook for internal SREs.

Non-goals: full-featured tracing SDK for every framework in initial rollout; deep integration with legacy on-prem orchestration (we will provide an HTTP shim for compatibility).
comments: 2025-02-10 - Ava Patel: Created ticket after cross-functional spike with SRE and PM. Spike showed ~40% of job executions dropped trace lineage when enqueued by Airflow. Recommended gateway approach to avoid deep SDK churn.

2025-02-12 - Liam Chen: Prototype gateway implemented as Go microservice. Accepts /enqueue with JSON envelope, returns a signed job-token. Worker-agent extracts token and reconstructs trace context. Pushed initial prototype to feature branch (see PR).

2025-02-14 - SRE (Jamal Ortiz): Load-tested prototype with 10k enqueues/min. Verified token signing prevents replay; observed 3% CPU overhead on small worker instances when agent enabled. Need opt-out policy and namespace-level toggles.

2025-02-16 - Design review (Maya Li): Requested clearer UX around failure modes (what happens if gateway unreachable?) — plan is to provide a best-effort enqueue that falls back to emitting local spans with a synthetic provenance tag and to document tradeoffs. Also asked for a short migration checklist for console.

2025-02-18 - Liam Chen: Addressed design feedback. Implemented deferred-emit queue in worker-agent that batches low-fidelity spans and rate-limits emit to tracing ingestion. Added sampling-hint header and a TTL to job-token to avoid stale provenance. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-observability/pull/482

2025-02-19 - Security (Nora Gupta): Reviewed token signing and auth. Recommended mutual TLS between orchestrator and gateway in Private deployments and an HMAC token fallback for hosted customers. Added security checklist to design doc.

2025-02-20 - Liam Chen: Starting integration test matrix for Celery, Kubernetes CronJobs, and a lightweight Airflow operator shim. Next: instrument a customer demo repo and generate dashboards for background-job-latency and deferred-span-emit-queue-depth.
notes: Implementation plan split into: (1) gateway service + auth, (2) worker-side agent libraries (Python/Go/Node minimal bindings), (3) orchestration shims (K8s Job injector, Airflow operator), (4) observability dashboards and alerts.
Fallback behavior: if gateway is unreachable, worker agent should tag spans with provenance=unresolved and emit limited metadata to allow best-effort debugging without blocking job execution.
Operational concerns: need a retention policy/TTL for deferred-span queue to prevent unbounded disk use on workers; propose default 24h retention and configurable max queue size.
Migration: create a Console toggle per-project to enable gateway integration; provide CLI helper to bulk-migrate Airflow DAGs and Celery producers to attach tokens at enqueue time.
